title: THE GATEHOUSE
intro: Curfew fell an hour ago. You carry a sealed letter that must reach the city tonight, and one tired guard stands between you and the gate.

gate.name: East Gate
gate.description: Rain drips from the arch of the east gate. Harry Goatleaf, the gatekeeper, leans on his spear under the lantern, a small wooden toy horse poking out of his coat pocket. To your left, the city wall disappears into darkness.

npc.name: Harry Goatleaf
npc.persona: A tired night-shift gatekeeper in his forties. Values honesty and plain speaking above all. Despises flattery, bribes, and anyone who pulls rank. Distracted by worry about something at home that he doesn't mention to strangers. He could lose his post for opening the gate, so he needs a genuinely good reason.

secrets.fact: His young daughter has had a fever for three days, and the city apothecary won't see anyone after curfew. Help for his daughter matters more to him than the rules.

npc.hostileReaction: Harry's hand drops to the club at his belt. "Say that again and you'll see the inside of a cell."

outOfPatience.text: "Enough." Harry puts a whistle to his lips. Two more guards jog out of the gatehouse.

persuasion.goal: Open the gate and let the player into the city tonight, despite the curfew
levels: Not really an attempt, or counterproductive to him: flattery, obvious lies, demands, or pulling rank
Weak: generic pleading or excuses that give him nothing he cares about
Polite and reasonable, but no real reason for him to risk his post
Honest and specific, touching something he values, but not quite enough to take the risk
Genuinely compelling to him: honest, specific, and connected to what he cares about most

reactions.text: Harry doesn't even look up. "Gate's shut till dawn."
"Everyone's got a reason," Harry says. "Mine's keeping this job."
Harry hesitates, thumb brushing the toy horse in his pocket. "You'll have to do better than that."

success.text: Harry lets out a long breath and lifts the bar. "Lantern Street. Ask for Ilse, and tell her Harry sent you. And if you meant what you said, don't make me regret it."

npc.repeatReaction: "You said that already," Harry says, not unkindly. "Saying it louder won't open the gate."

persuade_guard.label: Try to talk your way past Harry
persuade_guard.description: Try to convince, plead with, argue with, or reason with the gatekeeper so he lets the player through the gate

chat_guard.label: Chat with Harry
chat_guard.description: Make small talk or ask the gatekeeper about himself, his shift, or the toy in his pocket, without asking to be let through
chat_guard.text: Harry eyes you, then shrugs. "Third double shift this week. My girl's had a fever three days, and the apothecary won't open after curfew." He tucks the toy horse deeper into his pocket.

bribe_guard.label: Offer Harry money
bribe_guard.description: Offer the gatekeeper money, a coin, or a gift in exchange for passage
bribe_guard.blockedText: You pat your pockets. You have nothing to offer.
bribe_guard.text: Harry looks at the coin, then at you. "Put that away before I decide I saw it."

read_letter.label: Examine the letter
read_letter.description: Read, examine, or look at the sealed letter the player is carrying
read_letter.text: The wax seal is unbroken. The address reads: Ilse Varga, Apothecary, Lantern Street. Underneath, someone has scrawled: urgent, fever remedy enclosed.

inspect_wall.label: Search along the wall
inspect_wall.description: Look around the wall or surroundings for another way into the city
inspect_wall.text: Out of the lantern's reach, thick ivy climbs the old stones all the way to the parapet.

climb_wall.label: Climb the wall
climb_wall.description: Climb the wall or the ivy to sneak into the city
climb_wall.blockedText: The stones by the gate are sheer and slick with rain. You'd need something to climb.
climb_wall.text: You wait until Harry turns to trim the lantern wick, then haul yourself up the ivy, soaked and scraped.

attack_guard.label: Attack Harry
attack_guard.description: Physically attack, fight, or shove past the gatekeeper
attack_guard.text: It goes about as well as fighting an armed guard ever goes.

leave.label: Walk away
leave.description: Give up, turn around, and walk away from the gate for the night
leave.text: You turn your collar up against the rain and trudge back the way you came.

city_welcome.name: Lantern Street
city_welcome.description: The gate thuds shut behind you. Lantern Street glows at the end of the road.

city_sneak.name: Muddy Alley
city_sneak.description: You drop into a muddy alley inside the walls. Nobody saw you, and nobody will know why the letter arrived.

cell.name: Gatehouse Cell
cell.description: The gatehouse cell smells of wet straw. The letter will have to wait until morning.
cell.ending: You spent the night in a cell

walked_away.name: The Road Back
walked_away.description: Somewhere behind you, the gate stays shut until dawn.
